name: arity
title: arity(f) -> number
description: Returns the number of parameters the given function f expects, excluding the rest parameter.

name: char_at
title: char_at(s, i) -> string
description: Takes a string s as first argument and a nonnegative integer i as second argument. If i is less than the length of s, this function returns a one-character string that contains the character of s at position i, counting from 0. If i is larger than or equal to the length of s, this function returns undefined.

name: display
title: display(v, s) -> value
description: Optional second argument. If present, displays the given string s, followed by a space character, followed by the value v in the console. If second argument not present, just displays the value v in the console. The notation used for the display of values is consistent with JSON, but also displays undefined, NaN, Infinity, and function objects.

name: error
title: error(v, s) -> undefined
description: Optional second argument. If present, displays the given string s, followed by a space character, followed by the value v in the console with error flag. If second argument not present, just displays the value v in the console with error flag. The evaluation of any call of error aborts the running program immediately. The notation used for the display of values is consistent with JSON, but also displays undefined, NaN, Infinity, and function objects.

name: get_time
title: get_time() -> number
description: Returns number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. See also textbook example.

name: Infinity
title: Infinity
description: The name Infinity refers to the special number value Infinity. See ECMAScript Specification, Section 4.3.23

name: is_boolean
title: is_boolean(v) -> boolean
description: checks whether a given value is a boolean

name: is_function
title: is_function(v) -> boolean
description: checks whether a given value is a function

name: is_number
title: is_number(v) -> boolean
description: checks whether a given value is a number. See also textbook example.

name: is_string
title: is_string(v) -> boolean
description: checks whether a given value is a string. See also textbook example.

name: is_undefined
title: is_undefined(v) -> boolean
description: checks whether a given value is the special value undefined

name: NaN
title: NaN
description: The name NaN refers to the special number value NaN ("not a number"). Note that NaN is a number, as specified by is_number. See ECMAScript Specification, Section 4.3.24

name: parse_int
title: parse_int(s, i) -> number
description:
Interprets a given string s as an integer, using the positive integer i as radix, and returns the respective value.
Examples: parse_int("909", 10) returns the number 909, and parse_int("-1111", 2) returns the number -15.
See ECMAScript Specification, Section 18.2.5 for details.

name: prompt
title: prompt(s) -> string
description: Pops up a window that displays the string s, provides an input line for the user to enter a text, a Cancel button and an OK button. The call of prompt suspends execution of the program until one of the two buttons is pressed. If the OK button is pressed, prompt returns the entered text as a string. If the Cancel button is pressed, prompt returns a non-string value.

name: stringify
title: stringify(v) -> string
description: returns a string that represents the value v, using a notation that is is consistent with JSON, but also displays undefined, NaN, Infinity, and function objects. See also textbook example.

name: undefined
title: undefined
description: The name undefined refers to the special value undefined. See also textbook explanation in section 4.1.1.
